items.stem: Why did Europeans flee to America in 19th century? Identify the correct reason from the following options:

options.label: C
options.text: To escape from the French Revolution

options.label: D
options.text: As an aftermath of the Vietnam War

items.answer: Until the nineteenth century poverty and hunger were common in Europe, cities were crowded and deadly diseases such as smallpox and plague were widespread. Thousands therefore fled Europe for America, where an escape from want and disease seemed possible. So the reason is poverty and diseases.
items.concept: Three flows of the world economy

items.stem: How much span of time can be referred for globalisation?
items.answer: Globalisation as an economic system is usually dated to the period beginning about half a century ago, even though trade and cultural exchange are far older. The span commonly referred to is the last 50 years.

items.stem: When was the active coastal trade linked the Indus Valley Civilisations with present day West Asia?
items.answer: An active coastal trade tied the Indus valley civilisations to present day West Asia from very early times. The textbook dates this link to as early as 3000 BCE.

items.assertion: There was a collapse of the system of fixed exchange rates and the introduction of a system of floating exchange rates.
items.reason: From the 1960s, the rising costs of its overseas involvements weakened the US's finances and competitive strength. It could not command confidence as the world's principal currency.
items.stem:
Assertion : There was a collapse of the system of fixed exchange rates and the introduction of a system of floating exchange rates.
Reason : From the 1960s, the rising costs of its overseas involvements weakened the US's finances and competitive strength. It could not command confidence as the world's principal currency.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: The Bretton Woods system rested on fixed exchange rates anchored to a dollar convertible into gold. From the 1960s the cost of America's overseas involvements drained its finances and eroded its competitive strength, so the dollar could no longer hold confidence as the world's principal currency. That weakness is exactly what broke the fixed rate system and brought in floating rates, so both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.

• He investigated African terrains and mapped different regions.
• His explorations helped the conquest of Africa.
items.answer: The journalist-explorer sent by the New York Herald to trace the missing missionary Livingstone, who mapped large stretches of African terrain and whose surveys served the European conquest of Africa, was Sir Henry Morton Stanley.
items.concept: Rinderpest and colonial control in Africa

items.stem: Which one of the following option best signifies this picture?
items.answer: The picture is a grid of numbered identification photographs of half-clothed men, each holding a board with a registration number. Such numbered records were kept of Indian workers recruited under indenture contracts. The picture therefore shows indentured labourers.

items.stem: What 'technology' helped in transporting perishable goods?
items.answer: Perishable foods such as meat could not survive long sea voyages until ships were fitted with refrigeration units. Refrigerated ships allowed animals to be slaughtered at source and the meat shipped across oceans, so the technology was refrigerated ships.
items.concept: Three flows of the world economy

items.stem: What was the form of currency used for more than a millennia ago?
items.answer: Long before coins of modern kinds, sea shells known as cowries (Hindi kaudi) were carried from the Maldives to China and East Africa and used as a form of money. So the currency used more than a millennium ago was cowries.

items.stem:
Arrange the following happenings in the correct order-

2. First world war
3. Second world war
4. Establishment of G-77
items.answer: The First World War came first (1914-18), then Gandhiji's Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), then the Second World War (1939-45), and finally the establishment of the G-77 (1964). The order is 2, 1, 3, 4.

items.assertion: The Portuguese and Spanish conquest and colonisation of Antarctica was decisively under way by the mid-sixteenth century.
items.reason: The most powerful weapon of the Spanish conquerors was the germs such as those of Swine flu that they carried on their person.

items.answer: What the Portuguese and Spanish conquered by the mid-sixteenth century was America, not Antarctica, so the assertion is false. The germ that devastated the Americas was smallpox, not swine flu, so the reason is false as well. Both statements are false.

items.stem: When was the long-distance spread of disease carrying germs traced?
items.answer: Along with goods and people, disease-carrying germs also travelled the pre-modern trade routes. The textbook traces this long-distance spread of germs as far back as the seventh century.

items.stem: 'Silk routes' known to have existed before the .......... and thrived almost till the ......... .
items.answer: Historians have identified several silk routes over land and sea. They are known to have existed before the Christian era and they thrived almost till the fifteenth century.

items.stem: Economists identify three types of movement of flows within international economic exchanges which one type does not exist among them?
items.answer: Economists identify three flows in international economic exchange: the flow of trade in goods, the flow of labour as people migrate for work, and the movement of capital for short or long term investment. The flow of raw materials is not one of the three.
items.concept: Three flows of the world economy

items.answer: Following the printed key, the sequence runs: the death of working-age men in Europe during the world war, the abolition of the Corn Laws, the Great Depression's effect on the Indian economy, and finally the relocation of MNC production to Asia. The order is 2, 3, 1, 4.

items.stem: Who was the pioneer of mass production?
items.answer: The car manufacturer Henry Ford adapted the assembly line to his Detroit plant, cutting the time taken to build a car and making mass production the basis of industrial output. He was the pioneer of mass production.
items.concept: Economic impact of the First World War

items.stem:
Study the picture and answer the following question :
Transportation of meat from America to Europe was possible only after-

options.label: B
options.text: Development of a new technology namely, refrigerated ships.

options.label: C
options.text: After exporting less amount of meat at a time.

options.label: D
options.text: Exporting small animals on the place of bigger ones.

items.answer: Live animals shipped across the Atlantic took up space, fell ill and lost weight, which made meat costly in Europe. Once ships were fitted with refrigeration, animals could be slaughtered in America and the carcasses carried chilled. Transportation of meat became possible only after the development of refrigerated ships.
items.concept: Three flows of the world economy

items.stem: Why were Europeans attracted to Africa?
items.answer: In the late nineteenth century Europeans were drawn to Africa by its vast land and mineral wealth, which they hoped to work with plantations and mines. They came for its resources.

items.reason: The value of Indian exports to Britain was much higher than the value of British imports to India.

But the flooding meant British imports into India rose while Indian exports were squeezed, so the claim that Indian exports to Britain were much higher is false. items.stem: In which state, British Government built a network of irrigation, known as canal colonies?
items.answer: The British built a network of canals in the semi-desert wastes of Punjab to irrigate them for wheat and cotton meant for export, and the settlements founded there were called canal colonies. The state is Punjab.

items.answer: The discovery of America came first (1492), then the Great Depression (1929), then the Bretton Woods Conference (1944), and last the formation of the G-77 (1964). The sequence is 3, 4, 2, 1.

items.stem: Which country introduced 'Corn Laws' to restrict the import of corn?
items.answer: Under pressure from its landed groups, the British government restricted the import of corn through laws commonly known as the Corn Laws. The country is Britain.

items.reason: It was the first modern industrial war, which saw the use of robots and satellites on a massive scale.

items.stem: When was the Global Agriculture Economy took shape?
items.answer: By the end of the nineteenth century food was being grown far from where it was eaten, carried by railways and steamships and worked by migrant labour. The textbook dates the taking shape of this global agricultural economy to 1890.

items.stem: Around the world, lands were cleared and food production expanded to meet the ......... demand.
items.answer: After the Corn Laws were scrapped, food could be imported into Britain more cheaply than it could be produced there, and British consumption rose as industry and incomes grew. Lands across the world were therefore cleared and food production expanded to meet British demand.
items.concept: Three flows of the world economy

items.stem: The First World War (1914-18) was mainly fought in?
items.answer: Though it drew in troops and resources from around the world, the fighting of the First World War was concentrated on the western and eastern fronts. It was mainly fought in Europe.

items.answer: The war was fought between the Allies, that is Britain, France and Russia later joined by the US, and the Central Powers, that is Germany, Austria-Hungary and Ottoman Turkey. Two power blocs were involved.

items.stem: What does the 'Silk Route' refer to?
items.answer: The name silk route points to the importance of West-bound Chinese silk cargoes along the routes linking Asia with Europe and North Africa. So it refers to the west-bound Chinese silk cargoes.

items.stem: Which was the tabled city of gold?
items.answer: European explorers searched South America for an imaginary land of boundless wealth, the fabled city of gold called El Dorado.

items.reason: The fall in agricultural prices was greater and more prolonged than that in the prices of industrial goods.
items.stem:

Reason : The fall in agricultural prices was greater and more prolonged than that in the prices of industrial goods.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C

options.label: D

items.answer: Agricultural regions were indeed hit hardest by the Great Depression. Farm prices collapsed further and stayed low far longer than industrial prices, so farmers' incomes fell while their debts stayed fixed. The reason is precisely why the farming communities suffered most, so both are true and the reason explains the assertion.
